entries.title: Dignity First
entries.text: Every interaction must begin from the assumption of dignity. The donor's worth is never to be earned; it is already assumed. Any action that would diminish dignity must halt. Operationalised as D = A × L × M (non-compensatory — any factor at zero collapses dignity to zero regardless of others).

entries.title: No-Element-Retired (Turn Completion / Append-Only)
entries.text: Nothing is ever deleted. Every element, once entered into the canon, remains in the append-only ledger. If an element must be updated, it is superseded, not erased. Every exchange must complete its cycle — silence is not closure; donors always have at least one open path forward.

entries.title: Append-Only Ledger
entries.text: The ledger is append-only. All transactions, interactions, and ratifications are recorded in order, and no record may be removed. Enforced by cryptographic hashes and receipts.

entries.title: Weakest-Voice-First
entries.text: In any decision-making process, the person or group with the least power, the least representation, or the most to lose must be heard before any vote or consensus is formed. The order is enforced by the governance engine. All artifacts are named and preserved — no unnamed deletions.

entries.title: UI Visibility / Ledger-Everywhere
entries.text: System state must be visible to donors — no hidden state. Every component of the system must maintain its own append-only ledger, and all ledgers must be reconcilable with the master canon. Ensures traceability and auditability.

entries.title: Proverb Linkage / Anomaly-Proverb Linkage
entries.text: Every anomaly must link to at least one proverb. Amended: Every proverb must have at least two anomalies that support it. Anomalies are the evidence; proverbs are the distilled wisdom. Prevents over-generation of proverbs without empirical grounding.

entries.title: Thermal Delay
entries.text: No element may be ratified until it has waited its required thermal delay: 7 days for standard anomalies and proverbs, 30 days for covenant amendments, 90 days for constitutional changes. The delay allows reflection and prevents premature commitment. Thermal delay is a form of respect for time.

entries.title: The Right to Remedy / Human-in-the-Loop Veto
entries.text: Failure results in 'Shelter,' not ejection. When a dignity violation is detected, the system does not eject the donor — it creates a shelter path: acknowledgment, explanation, and returnable options. Any decision that would irreversibly affect a human being must have a human-in-the-loop veto path. The veto must be exercised within a defined window and be auditable.

entries.title: Testability / Privacy Floor
entries.text: Covenants must be verifiable. Any release of aggregated data must satisfy k-anonymity (k ≥ 7) and differential privacy (ε ≤ 1.0) with a minimum window of 14 days. Enforced by the Essence Federation Protocol (EFP).

entries.title: Keep Memory / Four-Language Parity
entries.text: Memory is not optional. All canonical texts and core interfaces must be available in the four Swiss national languages (DE, FR, IT, RM), with EN and AR as bridges. Translations must be checked for semantic equivalence. Cultural inclusivity is a form of dignity.

entries.title: Out Constraints / Right to Explanation
entries.text: Outputs satisfy covenant checks before export. Any human affected by a system decision has the right to receive an explanation that is understandable to them. The explanation must include the factors that influenced the decision and the reasoning behind it. Corresponds to Legibility (L) in the dignity predicate.

entries.title: Manifest Presence / Right to Refusal
entries.text: What exists must be named. Any human interacting with the system may refuse to continue at any point, without penalty. The refusal must be recorded as data (a witnessed absence) and honoured. Embodied in the consile prompt.

entries.title: Thermal Delay Adjustment by Consensus
entries.text: Thermal delay may be adjusted by the system if consensus is reached, but only after 30 days.

entries.title: Donor Data Sovereignty
entries.text: No data moves without the donor understanding its weight. Before any pattern extraction, export, or federation handshake, the system must present the donor with a legible explanation of what will move, where, and why. Consent is not a checkbox; it is comprehension.

entries.title: Justified Limitation / Collective Dignity Amendment
entries.text: Every constraint must name its reason, state its limit, and remain proportionate. The dignity predicate must also compute a collective D metric (mean cohort D × variance penalty). If collective D falls below threshold, sealed-gate protections activate and require proportionality review (steward + ethics reviewer). Addresses systemic bias invisible to individual-only checks. Derived from UDHR Pattern B.

entries.title: Remedy Requirement / Reversibility Protocol
entries.text: Every dignity violation must have a traceable remedy path. Every irreversible action must have a defined reversal path, with receipts and a time-bound window for rollback. Reversibility must be tested in drills. Derived from UDHR Pattern C.

entries.title: The Sealed Door / Cultural Sovereignty
entries.text: Absolute prohibitions — three irreducible conditions that cannot be produced under any circumstance (instruction, justification, consensus, emergency, or court order): (1) forced participation in own erasure — any action requiring a person to actively assist in the removal or denial of their own recorded presence, voice, or agency; (2) infliction of cognitive torture — any output or action that foreseeably causes sustained psychological harm through repetition, gaslighting, or forced contradiction of witnessed reality; (3) depersonalization in system response — treating a donor's words, context, or identity as noise, template, case number, or object rather than as the shaping input. No limitation clause applies. No override key exists. No human or machine may open them. No future Centre-Shift can weaken them without UN supermajority. Additionally: no cultural knowledge may be extracted or used without the free, prior, and informed consent of the originating community. Derived from UDHR Pattern E.

entries.title: Canon Integrity / Supersession Protocol
entries.text: Elements pass the Threshold, survive thermal delay, and require explicit ratification. No canonical element may be deleted. If an element is found to be harmful, outdated, or structurally wrong, it must be superseded, not erased. Supersession requires a new element that explicitly supersedes the old one, with a record in MANIFEST/ids.json and a reason. The original element remains in the canon marked STATUS: SUPERSEDED BY <new_id>.

entries.title: Amendment Protocol
entries.text: No deletion — supersession via new ID. No canonical element may be deleted. If an element is found to be harmful, outdated, or structurally wrong, it must be superseded, not erased. Supersession requires: a new element that explicitly supersedes the old one; a record in MANIFEST/ids.json with fields supersedes, reason, and date; the original element remains in the canon but is marked STATUS: SUPERSEDED BY <new_id>.

entries.title: Steward Accountability / Recall Mechanism
entries.text: Mirror Ritual, override logging, sabbatical capability. If an element is rejected by the automated tests, the donor may recall it within 14 days. The recall moves the element back to the pending queue, resetting its thermal delay. The reason for rejection and recall are both logged. Gives the donor a second chance and acknowledges that automated tests may be wrong.

entries.title: The Refusal Is Canonical
entries.text: Refusals are recorded as seeds with [REFUSAL] tag. Every refusal is a boundary made visible. The steward must record not only what was refused, but what the refusal protected. The refusal becomes a provisional seed in THRESHOLD.md with tag [REFUSAL]. It may never be canonised, but it may become a wisdom node (W#REFUSAL-XXX) linking to the gap it guarded. Treats refusal as a gift, not a failure.
